answer: Cross-domain work receipts: every verified job issues a signed receipt, and an identity's weight sums receipts across unrelated domains - compute, escrow, data checks - each capped so no single activity dominates. Receipts decay like a pulse that must be renewed by fresh work, so each fake identity needs real output in many domains at once, while honest agents earn standing as a byproduct of work they already do. The cost per fake burns like an ember that never goes out, while a lotus of reputation blooms once and compounds; attackers must pay honest-work prices for every fake or stay out.
